reviews.text: If I could only use one word to describe The Woman King as a historical action epic, it would be “quintessential”.
reviews.author: Joseph Tomastik

reviews.text: The Woman King is more than just a historical action film; it is a genuinely rare example of breathing life into the past with verve and imagination.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: There’s a certain tenderness yet mightiness with which director Prince-Bythewood choses to frame the story visually. Her exceptional direction enables an experience that is as emotionally invigorating as it is empowering and inspirational.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: To see Black women at the centrepiece of a Hollywood epic like this is both refreshing and extremely overdue.
reviews.author: Shakyl Lambert

reviews.text: writer Dana Stevens, story contributor Maria Bello – more known for her acting (“A History of Violence”) – and Prince-Bythewood continue an emerging cinematic trend of alternate, redemptive histories that bend toward utopianism
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Davis elevates this standard story with the emotion and dire she brings to her performance.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: For viewers who choose to focus on the adrenaline rush of the feminist warriors ready to challenge the patriarchy, The Woman King proudly wears its crown.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: Thuso Mbedu delivers one of the best feature film debut performances I've ever witnessed. The anti-slavery, anti-racism and equal human rights messages are well conveyed, but the authentic, emotionally resonant character dynamics stand out.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: While this is undoubtedly Viola Davis at her finest, the movie's breakout star is Thuso Mbedu as Nawi. It may be called The Woman King, but it's Mbedu that steals the spotlight in every frame.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: An instant classic, Viola Davis slays as always. Lashana Lynch is incredible, Sheila Atim is amazing, & Thuso Mbedu steals the show as the heart/soul of the entire film! Blythewood created an epic that we don’t see anymore from Hollywood.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Despite stumbles in terms of plot and pacing, The Woman King is a thrilling watch. This story, these women, and the film’s heart deserve to be seen on the biggest screen possible with an audience ready to go along for a wild ride.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: The movie fails to fulfil its potential except as a military action epic.
reviews.author: Whang Yee Ling

reviews.text: A dazzler from Terence Blanchard’s symphonic score to Polly Morgan’s eye pleasing cinematography. Acting is A-1, particularly by Davis and Mbedu.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: Viola Davis is a force unleashed, heading up a full-blooded tale of conflict set against the backdrop of the slave trade that offers both a twist on the traditional male-dominated warrior-epic and a look at a part of history Hollywood typically ignores
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Its the emotional sparring between the women - as fierce as anything on the battle ground - that really holds the attention
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: If it had been a story about white people, it would have been a snore. But we have rarely, if ever, seen a movie quite like this one about powerful Black women, and the energy onscreen is infectious.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: …goes all in as a popular entertainment, rolling back the male-dominance of the action genre and replacing it with something smart, dynamic and female driven…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: As these women take their place in the kingdom of Dahomey and assert their power, The Woman King truly takes on new meaning, and finds relevance in the modern era.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: The film is shot impeccably well, scored passionately, and gives the viewer something to savor as they leave the theater.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: It's not a perfect film but acting-wise - this is a masterclass. Pacing was tight and effective despite lacking in some character development. This is a really good film.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: The performances, action scenes and cinematography were fantastic. I think the representation of bad ass black women was incredible.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Pacing issues and historical inaccuracies aside, The Woman King has great action and moving characters brought to life by a fantastic ensemble cast.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: A giddy mix of history and fantasy.
reviews.author: Scroll Staff

reviews.text: ...as a piece of entertainment, The Woman King works very well. The action is extremely well-staged and is visceral and brutal and endlessly fun.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: A wildly watchable and compelling movie, one of 2022's best popcorn films.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Between the historical African ballad and the feminist epic, The Woman King advances unspectacularly academic, annoyingly predictable, and blatantly contrived.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Gina Prince-Bythewood’s film offers all the pleasures of an old-school epic but with a fresh take—the heroes in this film are Black women, led by Viola Davis in an inspiring performance as the military leader Nanisca.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text:
The Woman King is a powerful film with Viola Davis playing and incredible lead. 

The dedication and craft put into this film is evident with strong performances and thoughtful moments.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: Gina Prince-Bythewood directs the best battle epic since “Braveheart” and “Gladiator." It's that good, applying a diverse cast to good old-fashioned spectacle storytelling. Is it revisionist history? Of course, but it's still the best movie of the year.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Gina Prince-Bythewood’s action flick stars a number of young actresses joining the ranks of Agojie, but Mbedu really kills it with plenty of stunts and an emotional tale of mothers and daughters.
reviews.author: Fletcher Peters

reviews.text: The Woman King is one of the best films of 2022! Viola Davis commands this film with her presence of power & emotional grace. Every other cast member are just as powerful & engaging. Amazing dedication to scripting, choreography, stunt work, & directing
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: Films often elect spectacle or substance. To its credit, The Woman King offers both in a rousing tale of women warriors while mounting a devastating historical and cultural critique.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: A rousing saga.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Poignant, proud, and powerful. What is remarkable is that this story has never been told in such magnitude and is a feat worthy of all the history books.  The strength in combat matched the strength in will.
reviews.author: Reginald Ponder

reviews.text: Viola Davis has her second-best role to date (love Ma Rainey) as Nanisca, the kick-ass and fearless leader. Lashana Lynch kills (literally and figuratively) as Nanisca's loyal lieutenant.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: I applaud the femme-focus of “The Woman King” and its depiction of strong-willed, strong-bodied women who earned their place of power.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: But the main selling point of The Woman King is its performances, with Davis and John Boyega standing out as especially phenomenal in this film.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: An epic story that gets lost in an uneven and bloated film encumbered by subplots that lead nowhere. Fortunately, the collection of misfires doesn't get in the way of enjoying this old-fashioned production... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Rosado

reviews.text: The film is more notable for the story it tells rather than how it tells it, with numerous action and fight sequences that are as precise as they're devoid of personality... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: 'The Woman King' artfully and seamlessly blends some familiar movie genres — following in the tradition of big-screen sagas like Gladiator, Braveheart, and Last of the Mohicans — with a fresh female perspective. And, Viola Davis rules!
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: It does not seek to question masculinity, but limits itself to replacing the Leonids on duty with hypermasculinized women.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rubén Romero Santos

reviews.text: For all its formulaic plotting and pedestrian dialogue, The Woman King is fresh in every other way: Its visual palette, its setting and art direction, its voice and perspective. It’s as beautiful to look at as it is tonally fierce – as it is predictable
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Prince-Bythewood’s achievement is urgent, brilliant filmmaking and Davis’s performance is bound to become iconic.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: “Inspired by real historical events” means in Hollywood-speak: “A grain of truth in a bed of fiction and fantasy”
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Not that they have to here, but the phenomenal quartet that is Davis, Lynch, Mbedu and Atim could lift any material.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Just a good-old-fashioned swords-and-sandals epic told with a fresh, diverse spin. Viola Davis is a cannonball in this, which is the most interesting/best performance she’s given since Fences.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: The Woman King is a genuine crowd-pleaser that delivers grand entertainment in terms of blockbuster scale, punchy set-pieces and a formidable cast. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Set against a dark backstory, this exhilarating tale of Amazon women, brimming with female energy, has more going for it than most superhero flicks
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: In this sisterhood of soldiers there’s more empathy.  It’s not that they're weak, but that they understand the price of being strong.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: A wholly exciting feature that overcomes any conventionality with its fierce female spirit, and that’s more than enough to warrant a passionate celebration.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: The dialogue is generic -- the formal kind constructed to suit all periods -- but the actors give it all the authenticity it needs, clearly delighted by the ebullience of their characters.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: A big, mean, pulpy movie that drags the old Hollywood historical epic out of the shadows and into the cultural moment.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Stories of heroism, loyalty, implacable enemies and epic battles-to-win-the-day are as old as Hollywood. The Woman King makes the genre fresh again. Go and see it on the biggest screen you can find.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: A film you’re supposed to admire, never mind its obvious shortcomings...For all its claims of being an epic film, it's blighted by some pretty ordinary cinematography...The messy battle scenes look as though they were edited in a blender.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: An exciting character-driven spectacle of historical conflict, political machinations and heroism.
reviews.author: Thomas Caldwell

reviews.text: Everything -- performances, costumes, score, swashbuckling choreography, courtly intrigue -- comes together, as Dana Stevens’ screenplay hits all the right notes.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Emotional and gripping
reviews.author: Derek Sante

reviews.text: With great visuals and choreography making each battle a physically brutal dance, we get a sense of what these women are fighting for whether "each other" means the Agojie or Africa itself.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: The cinematography is what makes the film a success. The direction, the acting, the action and the execution are all flawless, just like the women themselves.
reviews.author: Nabila Hatimy

reviews.text: It is a film designed to inspire audiences and elicit cheers and, by and large, it succeeds.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Technically, The Woman King is an accomplished historical epic that doesn’t stray too far from the formula. However, the real life grounding and the strength of the performances make it one of 2022’s most rewarding surprises.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: The Woman King accomplishes a magnificent feat: delivering an epic, action-packed tale without sacrificing character development.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Roberto Landaverde

reviews.text: Exhilarating, suspenseful and moving, The Woman King is an epic action film that celebrates the power of women.
reviews.author: Ayelet Dekel

reviews.text: The Woman King engagingly blends fiction and historical fact into a thematically rich deeply nuanced story of coming-of-age, finding your center, then choosing how you’ll stand your ground.
reviews.author: Ro Moore

reviews.text: In the case of The Woman King, we have anti-history mobilized in the selfish interests of an upper-middle class milieu, rewriting the past for money and status.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: The Woman King provides a template for how men can advocate for women.
reviews.author: Carolyn Hinds

reviews.text: In short, filmmaker Gina Prince-Bythewood and a stellar cast bring the legendary Agoji warrior women to life.
reviews.author: Ray Gill Jr.

reviews.text: 2022 is proving to be the year of female-driven narratives...but The Woman King brings it to another level that celebrates Black women through its power, pride and poise to create one of the best films this year.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Every historical epic needs a central, larger-than-life character and star to match. As General Nanisca... Viola Davis delivers a groundbreaking performance proving that she has yet to reveal the full gamut of her acting capabilities.
reviews.author: Razmig Bedirian

reviews.text: Thankfully, all flimsiness in the screenplay is overcome by the director, Gina Prince-Bythewood, and her committed cast, who transform a familiar dramatic milieu (Mulan meets Gladiator meets Wonder Woman) into thrilling, amphetamine-rush cinema.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Yes, the Woman King could be filed under wish-fulfilment, but that’s true of so many action classics.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A great time at the movies. A rare cinematic event.
reviews.author: Rogan Graham

reviews.text: With its slickly orchestrated violence, epic battle scenes and achingly cool heroes, this rousing crowd-pleaser is also this year’s most thrilling action movie.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: The appeal of this film, directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, derives entirely from its reversal of gender assumptions.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The end result is a novel, representation-stretching enterprise that, paradoxically, plays like the “sort of film they don’t make any more”.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: exemplary intersectional feminist call to arms for the African sisterhood to keep building on the achievements of their female ancestors & to keep fighting – & dancing – as they did, or might have done... with or without the approval of their patriarch
reviews.author: Anton Bitel

reviews.text: A breathless, thought-provoking and often brilliant movie that is determined to embolden end educate those watching it.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: While the story sees the state draw back from involvement in the slave trade, questions of complicity still linger more than most popcorn movies would allow.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A first-rate epic combining commanding performances and storming action with a powerful story.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: The Woman King isn’t intended to be any ordinary account of history. It is a vibrant, restorative celebration of Black womanhood in all its glory.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: The film uses history as a jumping off point for myth-making and in the process delivers an all-out action spectacle, just from a perspective movies have tended to ignore.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: This is a grand spectacle with vivid and theatrical performances.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Fierce, full of action and drama, "The Woman King" is yet another platform to showcase the amazing talent of Viola Davis.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: The Woman King is cinema at its finest. It speaks to a generation who understands the importance of representation and couples that enthusiasm as an unapologetic celebration of Black womanhood.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: A thunderously cinematic good time: see it on the biggest screen you can find.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: To get complex, scheming, heroic and strong black characters -- exhibiting much of what it means to be black on screen -- within the context of a historical movie is a treat.
reviews.author: Theolin Tembo

reviews.text: The fight choreography is stunning, with Prince-Bythewood showcasing the abilities of her performers in shots that grab hold of your eyeballs and refuse to let go.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Unlike the all-too-common, typically lazy "girl power" tropes found in your average blockbuster, director Gina Prince-Bythewood not only respects her female characters, but also cares for them as complex and flawed people.
reviews.author: Sarah Jessica Rintjema

reviews.text: Viola Davis introduced this film by calling it her magnum opus--and she was not kidding.  As the aging but brave warrior at the center of the film, she makes what should have been a mundane war movie something much more memorable
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Predictable script hitting every conventional beat... It all plays out like a Disney movie made for kids, except with copious throat slitting – and even that is relatively tame in order to maintain the PG-13 rating
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: The battles are exciting yet human-scaled, unlike those in today's blockbusters; injuries feel real.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: All in all, The Woman King is an exciting, action-packed, history-based melodrama with a new and unusual setting, gorgeous look and sound, and dynamic performances -- but with occasional jarring flaws in the script.
reviews.author: Monica Reid

reviews.text: But The Woman King is at its most powerful when it focuses on the army of women who don’t have superpowers but rely on training, strategy and unity.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Echoes of Gladiator and Braveheart resonate here almost deliberately, The Woman King surrenders to narrative conventions and clichés, seeking the safest paths... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: Phenomenal performances elevate a script that leaves much to be desired, falling back on its impressive action sequences to satisfy and entertain.
reviews.author: Rhys Bowen Jones

reviews.text: An action film of the times that doesn't quite serve the slightly touched upon themes -- machismo, slavery -- with a far-fetched romantic story...
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: It’s fast, and it’s loose, and it totally works.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Prince-Bythewood celebrates these women warriors through impressive fight scenes that are athletic but realistic, eschewing the sort of CGI overkill that has run rampant in recent action films.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: The Woman King is a crowd pleaser at its core, intent on entertaining the audience as much as elevating a story that many in its audience may not know (though they’ll probably still need to do a bit of research).
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: A welcome rarity in an audiovisual industry that's clearly seeking to update their outlook and stories. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: The Woman King is a rousing battle epic that wears its heart on its sleeve.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: The Woman King has two unnecessary plot points that distract from the power of the story of the Agojie.
reviews.author: Sa'iyda Shabazz

reviews.text: If you're someone who loves action movies that use "true events" as an entry to a deeper narrative about surviving trauma, defying misogyny and overcoming personal torment in the face, along with all the ass-kicking, then The Woman King is a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Melanie McFarland

reviews.text: A wildly entertaining feminist historical action film that delivers audiences a different kind of onscreen hero.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Let's get the Viola Davis Cinematic Universe started ASAP, please.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: The diffuse storytelling somewhat dilutes the film's themes but Viola Davis, a Terence Blanchard score and an inherently interesting milieu are all good reasons to see it.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: It’s Ms. Davis’s weary but firm insistence on always doing the right thing that carries the movie. She is as much of an action star here as Harrison Ford or Sylvester Stallone ever was.
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: Viola Davis is a force of nature and she proves it over and over  in this film.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Gina Prince-Bythewood films through the lens of Blackness, highlighting the beauty, strength, and fierceness of Black people, unlike most stories about the slave trade that wallow in Black trauma...
reviews.author: Sheri Flanders

reviews.text: Come the end of year awards, don’t be surprised to see Davis and co on those podiums because The Woman King might very well be one of the best movies you’ll see this year.
reviews.author: Daryl MacDonald

reviews.text: The Woman King has the feel of a Game of Thrones episode edited for the Lifetime Channel.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: "The Woman King," another world premiere movie from Toronto, has Viola Davis portraying a real warrior and ruling her historically accurate, all-female army the same way she dominated the recent opening weekend of the film festival there.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: It’s no surprise that Davis knocks it out of the park as the anchor of a strong film that deftly balances stellar action sequences with a strong emotional story.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Maybe Prince-Bythewood has tapped into something that the two lousy Wonder Woman movies missed, but whatever it is, it isn’t excitement. Her battle scenes are haphazard, with poor continuity.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: As if we needed something else to confirm Viola Davis’ place in the shrine of truly remarkable actresses, along comes The Woman King, an elaborately choreographed historical epic in which she towers over nearly every aspect of the film’s production.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Prince-Bythewood has made some wonderful films, but The Woman King may be her very best.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: The Woman King plays like old-fashioned, crowd-pleasing entertainment. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Viola Davis and Thuso Mbedu give excellent performances, powering the emotional center of this story. The battle scenes are well choreographed by Filip Ciprian Florian of Monster Hunter.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The sheen of a lot of this invariably feels more Hollywoodesque than something truly Pan-African. “The Woman King” filters Africa through a very specific lens of Hollywood, but it’s personal and visceral enough that it's exuberance is irresistible.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Prince-Bythewood continues to show her mastery of the "women kicking ass" action thriller. Viola Davis rules but Lashana Lynch also deserves a shout out for her balance of comedy, drama, and badassery.
reviews.author: Dana Han-Klein

reviews.text: The kind of nuanced tapestry of the female experience that can only come from a movie centered around multiple women rather than just one.
reviews.author: Caroline Siede

reviews.text: The cast is uniformly strong and the action scenes make fine use of its sound and editing to mask its PG-13 trappings
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: There’s no doubt that Gina Prince-Bythewood’s historical epic derives its strength from the terrific cast.   Viola Davis is a tour de force but with so many good performances, this is an ensemble piece whose strength lies in numbers.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: If you had any doubt that women over 55 can be fierce warriors, seeing Michelle Yeoh in Everything Everywhere All at Once and now Davis in The Woman King should disabuse you of that uncertainty.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: The Woman King at once feels like a pleasantly nostalgic throwback to a bygone era where historical epics reigned supreme and a bold step in an exciting new direction.
reviews.author: Melanie Fischer

reviews.text: This movie's true strength is in what says about the importance of female power today.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: A huge spectacle... African in nature but universal in its depiction of greed, suppression and tyranny. A deft team of female artists have masterfully created a feminist allegory that will excite and inform movie lovers for years to come.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: All you need to know about The Woman King: There’s Viola Davis, buff as an Olympian, a blood-stained panga machete slung over her shoulder, and an expression on her face that says, “Who’s next?”
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: One of the best films of the year and an exhilarating movie-going experience! The direction, acting and overall execution elevates this contained blockbuster to award-season frontrunner. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: A welcome widening of history...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: There's a lot going on in here... you want more time in this world. It's not completely brisk, but it feels like there's something else missing.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: It's worth checking out for Davis' performance alone, and the rest will hopefully garner enough attention to ensure it becomes the classic it deserves to be.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: The Woman King weaves story into history and brings to life the oft-forgotten prowess of this strong, female troop ... Even the staunchest fan of that Mel Gibson Scot movie will warm up to the new warrior king in town.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Where “The Woman King” excels is in tackling sisterhood, submission and defiance, while putting on a display of brute, female force.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Viola Davis and Thuso Mbedu are spectacular together, and the choreography showcased during some of these fights scenes is fantastic. This is an awe-inspiring experience that will have you on the edge of your seat.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: The Woman King is one of the year’s best films!
reviews.author: Dorian Parks

reviews.text: Led by beautiful performances, including award-worthy work from Viola Davis, The Woman King is a must-watch historical epic and needs to be experienced on the largest screen possible.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: The visual richness brought forth by Gina Prince-Bythewood doesn't quite salvage the simpleness of the premise. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: "...many of these details that stick out like a sore thumb to me are things most audiences may be unaffected by. The Woman King does a good enough job at curating rousing moments that many will find it easy to forgive or overlook the film’s flaws."
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: The battle scenes are beautifully mounted and really compelling.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: There is such muscularity, athleticism, and ballet [to the choreography]. It is just great.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: I’ve truly never experienced anything like it, as it manages to be both intimate and epic while staging some of the finest action sequences you will see this year. I can easily see this one cracking my Top 10 of the year list.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: With a swaggering walk and steely gaze, Davis mixes indomitable will and commitment to principle.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: The results provide a thrilling blend of grand, old-school entertainment and impactful storytelling.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, who cannot be pigeonholed, the film is a throwback of sorts to the big, exciting, emotional warrior epics that used to be all too common at the multiplex, with the twist that it’s women not men driving the action.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: A powerful film about sisterhood, family and unity that’s entertaining and educational.
reviews.author: Wilson Morales

reviews.text: The Woman King is the rare Hollywood movie that’s honest about the trauma of sexual violence that isn’t simultaneously rife with violently depressing storytelling.
reviews.author: Kylie Cheung

reviews.text: Thanks to Prince-Bythewood, Stevens, and some truly superb performances, I cared deeply about these fierce, courageous women. And when that’s the case, it’s a lot easier to look past the film's blemishes.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: It’s a well-crafted big screen event movie that stands out from this year’s pack of blockbusters for its context, if not for its content. And, frankly, that’s more than enough.
reviews.author: Dylan Roth

reviews.text: A rousing motion picture filled with well-choreographed battle scenes effectively folded into stories of human interest.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Gina Prince-Bythewood is up to the challenge of delivering a visually resplendent, crowd-pleasing spectacle that’s easy to recommend and even easier to love.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The Woman King has some genuine conflict, emotional weight and characters that aren't just 1-dimensional "strong female leads".
reviews.author: Adam Olinger

reviews.text: It’s awe-inspiring to see these women, particularly women of colour, radiating so much power and conviction that it emanates from the screen and washes over the audience.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: As Nanisca, (Viola) Davis would give Keanu Reeves’ John Wick pause. She is a battle-scarred, muscular, no-nonsense leader who does not mollycoddle her troops nor fear speaking truth to power. ...
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: The Woman King is tailored for entertaining audiences.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Director Gina Prince-Blythewood and her production team create a meticulously detailed West African world with a story that's dramatically propelled by Viola Davis' intense performance.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Davis brings a melancholy to her character that’s more complicated than the movie around her aims to be.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Seeing these women in front of and behind the camera seize this opportunity to tell a little-known history of deep heroics is beyond valuable.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: The Woman King filled with my spirit and soul as Viola Davis lead an all-star cast of Black woman to a historic, ground breaking cinematic triumph of epic proportions. Not to mention it being done in tandem with Nicole Brown and Gina Prince-Blythewood!!!
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Viola Davis' performance puts an ordinary war movie in a class by itself...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: A good cast and well-choreographed action can’t save the unfocused script or the dreadful cinematography.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: A triumph! An exhilarating, empowering and rousing epic adventure grounded in humanity.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: It’s this combination of the softer quiet moments and the large-scale blockbuster action-type sequences that makes The Woman King a film that will sweep audiences of all kinds into its tale.
reviews.author: Nicole Ackman

reviews.text: The Woman King is a barn burner if you’re just looking for an invigorating night at the movies. But Prince-Bythewood’s real triumph is in grounding that sterling entertainment in a challenging dramatic text.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: The temptation is to say it’s a David Lean-style adventure. It’s really a full-metal Gina Prince-Bythewood movie. Maybe "the" Gina Prince-Bythewood movie, given the way she’s marshaled all of her talents here.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: A fresh female perspective and a rich cultural texture boost this otherwise formulaic war epic, highlighted by a deeply felt portrayal from Viola Davis.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Every actor involved delivers career-best work, which makes the film’s aesthetic failings all the more disappointing.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The Woman King overcomes the perils of its overstuffed script with a collection of performances that elevate the whole.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: At the center, the true general, Prince-Bythewood, marshals every aspect of “The Woman King” in concert, conducting action, thrills and emotion beautifully. It is a remarkable, powerful film, and not to be missed.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Like Black Panther before it, The Woman King immerses us in African culture; only this time, it shifts the focus to real-life women and proves, without the corny factor, that we have always been warriors.
reviews.author: Carys Anderson

reviews.text: In a sea of soulless blockbuster action movies, it’s nice to see one with equal grit and soul. This is a triumphant historical epic where the quieter moments are as memorable as the rousing battle scenes. Viola Davis' magnum opus indeed.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: While the movie’s treatment is surprisingly conventional, the tale of women empowered to own their own bodies couldn’t be timelier.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: With The Woman King, director Gina Prince-Bythewood explores a neglected corner of history and has a ball doing it. Thanks to her quick pacing and impeccable staging of battle sequences, her enthusiasm is contagious.
reviews.author: Dan Lybarger

reviews.text: The movie is a rip-roaring riposte to the evils of colonialism, and it had the boisterous crowd at last week’s Toronto festival world premiere clapping and stomping in approval. And tears? There wasn’t a damp eye in the house.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: It is “Gladiator” or “Braveheart” but with a better lead and improved action. It is, hilariously, also almost a direct mirror of the plot from “Top Gun: Maverick.” Yet, for some reason, big fans of that movie aren’t as vocal proponents of this one…
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Movies are at their best when they make you feel something, and I had tears in my eyes throughout The Woman King. Viola Davis's layered performance of stoicism and fierceness is one of her best, but it's the incredible Lashana Lynch who steals the movie.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: This is an action spectacle with a beating heart.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: It’s only thanks to Davis' considerable efforts that The Woman King holds together.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Viola Davis is the central figure, Lashana Lynch steals the show, and John Boyega struts in director Gina Prince-Bythewood’s homage to African resistance and ‘90s historical epics.
reviews.author: Kevin Fox Jr.

reviews.text: The Woman King is a must-watch. An epic blockbuster unlike any other before it. From its amazing framing and visuals to its tightly directed story, it’s a riveting experience from beginning to end. It’s visceral, raw and groundbreaking in a lot of ways.
reviews.author: Shah Shahid

reviews.text: An action-packed, exciting, and even emotionally gripping tale.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: A fierce Viola Davis headlines this historical epic about women warriors in 1823 West Africa and reminds us how truly inspiring it is to see these brave sisters doing it for themselves.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Gina Prince-Bythewood’s take on the historic warrior women of Africa is a superhero epic but with living, breathing, relatable humans. Fight sequences are epic, the emotional framework deep, anchored by Viola Davis as power personified.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Middling historical epic anchored by dynamite performances.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Davis’ performance, and the ferocious fight scenes, make The Woman King worth watching.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Tells an obscure lesson in African history that needed to be told.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: “The Woman King” lets its excellent cast weave between hubris, shakiness, and strength, achieving not just richer representation but more thrilling fight scenes, too.
reviews.author: Joy Ashford

reviews.text: “The Woman King” is a dynamic epic that lives up to its regal title.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: The Woman King is a quintessential historical action epic.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: The film is a historical action epic that, for all the novelty of its setting and subservience to contemporary attitudes, traffics in a lot of cliché narrative beats and ideologies.
reviews.author: Kenji Fujishima

reviews.text: The Woman King is an enthralling film, mostly thanks to some dynamic sequences and winning performances.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: Complications of history aside, The Woman King is Black Panther minus the vibranium and with more women warriors, an empowerment tale fueled by kickassery, with battle scenes, ear-splitting ululated war cries and sword fights.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: The Woman King proves to be anger-inducing and surprisingly uplifting. Dealing with those two emotions in a film with such hefty subject matter might seem contradictory, but actually, in The Woman King, they belong together.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: It’s hard to understate how crushingly mediocre The Woman King is even comparison to its mid-budget historical epic kin.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: That women can be powerful isn’t news, and Ms. Prince-Bythewood is so focused on making her Amazons amazing that she forgets to make them interesting.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: The Woman King is radical, radiant, and riveting.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: See it as many times as your budget will allow, The Woman King gives us new heroes to cheer for and enough action to fuel new dreams.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Although it had me wondering about the real history, why shouldn't the ladies facing colonialists get their turn for revisionism? The action is decent & it's is one of the sweat-iest in memory, like a gladiator film. Warriors are doing it for themselves!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: It tells an important story. But it's like the live-action version of a Disney animated film that does not exist (yet). Screenplay is shallow and at times silly.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Rises to the challenge of using an old-fashioned template to deliver a floodtide of exhilarating new images.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Despite being wobbly at times, in the end, this "King" finds its footing.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Viola Davis and the cast overpower the film’s shortcomings to deliver a crowd-pleasing, new type of historical war epic.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: ‘The Woman King’ dares to ask the question, “What if we gave Viola Davis a big sword?” More movies should do this.
reviews.author: Meg Shields

reviews.text: So long as you don’t take it as a history lesson, “The Woman King” works as a brawny Hollywood action epic of the old school, though one with a slant you won’t have seen before.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: The film... retains Prince-Blythewood’s commitment to character and to Black love, both platonic and romantic. It is her Hollywood opus, complete with the thrilling action set-pieces and swelling score to prove it.
reviews.author: Sarah-Tai Black

reviews.text: The kinetic action adventure “The Woman King” is a sweeping entertainment, but it’s also a story of unwavering resistance in front of and behind the camera.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Never underestimate the power of a woman…especially Viola Davis. Director Gina Prince-Bythewood makes her fierce starring in this brutal, heart-pounding action epic.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Somehow, the film manages to feel like a throwback to the action movies of old while featuring people who were seldom allowed to occupy prominent roles back then.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: The Woman King is an excellently crafted historical epic, brought together by powerful performances, dynamic directing, and beautiful cinematography.
reviews.author: Britany Murphy

reviews.text: There’s not a lot wrong with it. It looks beautiful, the costumes are gorgeous, the fight scenes are terrific, and there is a nice bit of gore.
reviews.author: Sarah Jane

reviews.text: The film insists that real empowerment can only exist in a world other than our own. That’s a strikingly radical message.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: The Agojie are regular women — though they are highly skilled ones who have endured arduous training. Their bodies are covered in scars. They die, they kill, they ache, they mourn — but they also laugh, dance and love. Gina Prince-Bythewood shows it all.
reviews.author: Patricia Puentes

reviews.text: THE WOMAN KING is a magnificent film --- so utterly beautiful and powerful.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: THE WOMAN KING is as exciting as it gets and as poignant as it is violent.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: There’s not just fighting, but also traditional dances, chanting and singing, celebrating and mourning. You will not find a more colorful representation of African life that has nothing to do with lynch porn. I cannot tell you how refreshing that is
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: The movie's existence is vital. Its execution, however, leaves a bit to be desired.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Could have used less of the turgid melodrama that clutters up so many other period pieces.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: For me, bringing the story of Nanisca and the Agojie to modern younger audiences is just as much an achievement as creating such an emotionally powerful film.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: What we really want to see is an athletic Viola Davis wielding a curved blade and vanquishing her foes. And when we see her in action, “The Woman King” is bloody marvelous!
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The Woman King”is a character driven epic, one that tempers the rousing action scenes with powerful interpersonal relationships to keep us engaged. It feels like an old-fashioned action movie, but with a fresh and fascinating update.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Viola Davis owns “The Woman King,” a movie every bit as majestic and monumental as its title implies.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: This is a film driven by what makes its characters and conflicts tick. It’s freely fictionalized, and some of it’s overpacked. But “The Woman King” feels human-made, not machine-learned.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: While the film features many scenes of battleground melees with swords and axes swinging and connecting, the violence in this story resides more in the human heart than in any weapon.
reviews.author: A.C. Koch

reviews.text: Viola Davis towers in a fierce and gut-wrenching portrayal of courage. The Woman King is literally unlike any film I have seen.  Davis and a sublime supporting cast grace a sweeping narrative that touches many difficult issues.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Offering complicated substance along with its spectacle, The Woman King is a thrilling film that will no doubt be a crowd-pleaser.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: Equally a thrilling historical epic and an intimate character study, it's both familiar and fresh with a superb ensemble cast and stellar production values.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: The epic story of African women warriors (aka Virgin Warriors) led by General Nanisca (the force known as Viola Davis) is Wonder Woman, Black Panther & The Ten Commandments rolled into a larger than life historical action drama.
reviews.author: T.J. Callahan

reviews.text: Phenomenal, strong awards contender for sure. A complex film with both great action & compelling drama, it doesn't shy away from the horrors of slavery & Africa's part in those atrocities. Probably the role of Davis' career, surrounded by a stellar cast.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: The Woman King is a winning combination of drama and thrilling action.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Surface-level feminist subtext gives [The Woman King] a pass to indulge the same conventional clichés as other films of its ilk...[but] the formulaic action and predictable storytelling beats...are now in service of a lot of Disney-fied girlboss energy.
reviews.author: Paul Attard

reviews.text: The Woman King is yet more proof that, given the opportunity, women can perform as well — if not better — than their male counterparts at stereotypically male pursuits.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: It’s about mothers and daughters, about strength and power, and it is an absolute triumph. The Woman King stands above the rest.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: This film has a fire in its belly. But more importantly, it also has a heart full of love: love of life, love of freedom, love of Black people and culture, and love for its ferocious, complicated, brave women.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: Never underestimate the power of a woman, and that advice goes double when it comes to the powerhouse that is Viola Davis.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Whatever the occasional weaknesses of the script, "The Woman King" is never not engaging. The stakes are high and the villains clear, with enough dramatic subtlety to deepen the well of nuance.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: An exciting filmic experience full of action, feeling and many scenes of the great Viola Davis proving that she can kick butt as well as she can kick hearts. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Nobody will question the rousing cinematic throw-downs, but “The Woman King” offers little in the way of the honest and intimate character beats a movie like this needs in order to elevate it beyond the scope of the blunt and bloody action sequences.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: A well-acted, superbly made historical action flick that could easily serve as an inspiration for many in the same way we’ve seen from other films like it.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: A breathtaking, creative and powerful film.
reviews.author: Alexis Potter

reviews.text: The Woman King is the rare action drama that delivers both the sizzle and the steak.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: Prince-Bythewood is extremely focused on making a mostly overlooked tale of honor and dedication feel enormous and emotional.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The Woman King made me think of classic films like Spartacus and how they don’t make movies like this anymore. Then it also made me realize that they’ve never made movies like this for women of color, [. . .] a fresh take on a classic historical epic.
reviews.author: Megan McLachlan

reviews.text: A spirited and often thrilling action epic elevated by the regal, rigorous commitment of star Viola Davis.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The Woman King might on occasion follow something of a formula, but it's used to great effect, with terrific action, great performances, and a hefty story told with a deft hand.
reviews.author: Shelagh Rowan-Legg

reviews.text: With its epic tale of the solidarity that grows between the Dahomey as they battle against enslavement and exploitation, The Woman King illustrates, with stunning grace, how sisterhood can be more than dangerous and powerful.
reviews.author: Soraya Nadia McDonald

reviews.text: As The Woman King builds tension, it gains momentum while telling a unique story that is grand in scale, emotional at heart, and well executed.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Davis -- fierce and formidable, bruised and battle-scarred -- is a revelation...She proves that you don't have to look like Scarlett Johansson to be a female action hero.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Prince-Bythewood delivers the best film of her career thus far.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: While the story feels familiar, the perspective from which it is told is entirely fresh, making for a rare character-driven action epic that’s exhilarating and wholly unique in today’s cinematic landscape.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: It's frustratingly bloodless and narratively sanitized, but still with rousing, chest-beating action sequences and dynamite, powerful exchanges between Viola Davis and Thuso Mbedu
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The Woman King is a big, broad action epic that’s designed to be a crowd-pleaser.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Viola Davis showcases why she is such a powerhouse actor, displaying both fierce strength and heartfelt softness. Lashana Lynch, Sheila Atim, and Thuso Mbedu are the standouts, bringing an energy to the narrative that makes this a must-see movie.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: Prince-Bythewood offers audiences some interesting visuals and manages to make the fight scenes bloody and savage while not overselling the violence.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: A bold film that defies stereotypes and cliches, circumventing the obvious and giving us surprises and plot twists. Flawed human heroes without supernatural gifts, fighting evil and their own shortcomings to achieve a common goal—what a concept!
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: On one level, this is just a rousing Saturday-matinee action-adventure; on another, it carries the weight of everything Davis has done... and every page of Black history – Black women’s history – that hasn’t been told on this scale and in this medium.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: The Woman King is seriously entertaining action and packs an emotional punch.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: An African female warrior epic. Viola Davis handles an action hero role as deftly as she handles Oscar-nominated drama.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: It’s stirring but slightly stodgy, designed to stand the test of time.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Prince-Bythewood's directing style encompasses the perfect balance of action and drama.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: The Woman King is a sturdy, rousing piece of studio entertainment, that makes both the new feel old and the old feel new.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: It’s an oft-told tale, yes, but here imparted with a fresh angle and a meaningful moral.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: The Woman King is a film that has the confidence to be completely sincere in both the sharp moments of humor and the stunning battle sequences.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: “The Woman King” marks a ceasefire between two long-warring foes: Action and acting.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: The Woman King” is more than an action movie. It’s a film that depicts a side of African history that is rarely told and an opportunity for Black people to assert their humanity and regality.
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: Thrilling and enrapturing, emotionally beautiful and spiritual buoyant, The Woman King isn’t just an uplifting battle cry. It’s the movie Prince-Bythewood has been building toward throughout her entire career.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Viola Davis, who plays General Nanisca, called this film her magnum opus. And I would add that this indeed is the greatest performance of her career. Oscar voters everywhere should take note.
reviews.author: Jamie Broadnax

reviews.text: Consider the overall rating an average: The Woman King is an 8/10 for entertainment value, and 4/10 for how it deals with history.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: The Woman King leans toward fantasy in its heroic moments, but is rooted in truth about war, brutality and freedom. It is a splashy popcorn movie with a social conscience.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Energetic performances and technical precision come together to glorious effect in Prince-Bythewood’s rousing action film. It’s a lush, prime piece of entertainment in many respects.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

reviews.text: The film is bursting with remarkable elements: a vivid and fully realized setting, eye-popping battle sequences (pushing that PG-13 rating to wild ends), richly drawn characters, and wonderful performances from everyone.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: The Woman King delves into untold history for an effective action epic.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: The Woman King is sometimes cluttered and uneven, but the movie's compelling performances, gripping action, and inspiring personal stories can keep most viewers interested. Viola Davis is the movie's title character and should have been in more scenes.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The Woman King is a fantastic film that not only shows exactly why Gina Prince-Blythewood should helm action and drama alike, but also that Viola can easily best any action star on the screen.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: A rousing historical drama with great characters.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Extremely entertaining - Viola Davis totally reinvents herself in this one. A fascinating story beautifully brought to the screen.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

synopsis: The Woman King is the remarkable story of the Agojie, the all-female unit of warriors who protected the African Kingdom of Dahomey in the 1800s with skills and a fierceness unlike anything the world has ever seen. Inspired by true events, The Woman King follows the emotionally epic journey of General Nanisca (Oscar®-winner Viola Davis) as she trains the next generation of recruits and readies them for battle against an enemy determined to destroy their way of life. Some things are worth fighting for....
